newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian stocks charge ahead on dollar, Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian stocks charge ahead on dollar, Wall Street.

text.p: Norwegian shares powered a head for the third consecutive session on Thursday taking its lead from a firm dollar and the uptrend on Wall Street.
Dealer said the market would likely be hesitant ahead of Friday's U.S. unemployment data.

Oslo's Total share index advanced 1.46 percent to 1,095.13 points in bumper turnover of 1.23 billion crowns. The index has climbed almost four percent since Monday, strongly influenced by the blue chip stocks.
Trade on Thursday was heaviest in industrial giant Norsk Hydro and engineering and construction group Kvaerner, which together accounted for 220 million of the day's turnover.
Kvaerner's A share climbed 4.69 percent, of 16 crowns to 357 crowns, while the Bs were 15 crowns higher at 325 crowns, a day after the company announced that it was selling one of its cruise ships.
"The market has seen from the sale that Kvaerner is focusing on strategy. The disposal programme is on route," said one dealer.
